title: Role of Judiciary in Environmental Protection

content.overview: Indian courts have shaped environmental protection through constitutional interpretation (especially Article 21), recognition of principles such as precaution, polluter pays and public trust, and supervision of statutory compliance. The National Green Tribunal provides a specialised statutory forum under the NGT Act, 2010. High Courts under Article 226 and the Supreme Court under Articles 32 and 136 remain available where maintainable. Judicial intervention supplements but does not replace primary statutory regulation by Boards and the Central Government under the EPA, Water Act and Air Act.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Statutory forum (NGT/Board) available? (2) Constitutional writ maintainable? (3) Which principle is pleaded? (4) Relief sought — compliance, compensation, restitution?
content.study:
Route by forum first. NGT handles many Schedule I civil environmental questions; writ courts apply maintainability and alternative-remedy tests. Do not invent case holdings beyond retained migrated authorities in doctrine files.

Retained context cases in related topics: Vellore; M.C. Mehta line; Kamal Nath. No new case invented.

sections.heading: Constitutional jurisdiction
sections.body: Arts. 32 and 226 for fundamental-right and public-law environmental claims where maintainable; Art. 21 healthy-environment doctrine.

sections.heading: NGT
sections.body: Specialised tribunal — s. 14 jurisdiction, s. 15 relief, s. 20 principles (sustainable development, precaution, polluter pays).

sections.heading: Judicial principles
sections.body: Precautionary principle, polluter pays, public trust and sustainable development inform orders within the statutory and constitutional frame.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: Courts do not replace technical regulation; alternative remedies and maintainability constrain writ routes.

sections.heading: Coordination
sections.body: Board enforcement, EPA directions and NGT awards interact; choose the correct primary path on the facts.

examples.title: Choosing forum
examples.body: Industrial pollution victims may approach NGT under ss. 14–15 for compensation/restitution; a pure fundamental-right claim may still be tested under Art. 226/32 if maintainable.

hypotheticals.question: Must the High Court always hear an environmental PIL even when NGT has jurisdiction?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not necessarily. Alternative statutory remedy and maintainability analysis apply; NGT is the specialised forum for many Schedule I matters.

distinctions.title: NGT vs High Court environmental jurisdiction
distinctions.left: Statutory civil environmental questions under NGT Act ss. 14–15.
distinctions.right: Constitutional writ jurisdiction under Art. 226 — maintainability filters apply.

misconceptions.trap: Every environmental dispute must be filed only in the Supreme Court.
misconceptions.correction: NGT and High Courts are often the correct first forums depending on the claim and statute.
